headline_marked: [[Enterprise AI]] faces knowledge management challenges beyond context engineering
headline: Enterprise AI faces knowledge management challenges beyond context engineering
summary: Organizations are deploying more AI agents, leading to inconsistent knowledge representations and duplicated engineering efforts. A shared enterprise knowledge platform is needed to manage knowledge as a unified asset.
details: Current enterprise AI approaches often focus on context engineering for individual applications, leading to fragmented and inconsistent knowledge. This model struggles as organizations deploy multiple AI agents, each maintaining its own data pipelines and embeddings.

The core issue is not just providing context, but effectively managing enterprise knowledge itself. As AI applications proliferate, inconsistencies arise because different teams process the same documents, leading to conflicting understandings of business information.

Propagating changes becomes difficult when each application has its own context pipeline. Updates to documents or business definitions are not consistently reflected across all AI applications, causing them to operate on different versions of knowledge.

Organizations also face duplicated engineering efforts and increased costs as multiple teams rebuild similar knowledge pipelines, generate overlapping embeddings, and maintain separate indexes for different AI applications.

A shift towards a shared enterprise knowledge platform is proposed, analogous to enterprise data platforms. This platform would manage all enterprise knowledge as a unified asset, ingesting, organizing, integrating, and publishing reusable representations for every AI application.

This platform architecture separates knowledge management into four distinct layers: preserving raw information, normalizing it into managed knowledge objects, integrating it into a common enterprise knowledge model, and finally publishing optimized representations for AI applications.
caption:
Enterprise AI agents are only as reliable as the messiest documents behind them. The current context engineering approach is breaking down.
